review_candidates.title: IT Support Specialist
review_candidates.description: Description Title: IT Support Specialist Department: Business Support Team Location: Cleveland, Ohio Supervisor: Sr.IT Manager FLSA Status: Non-Exempt Position Status: Full Time Work Status (Remote/Hybrid/In-Office): Hybrid IT Support Specialist This is your chance to join the rapidly growing commercial solar energy business. FLEXRACK by Qcells is an integrated solar company that offers custom-designed, fixed tilt ground mount and single-axis solar tracking systems in the commercial and utility-scale solar mounting industries. FLEXRACK also offers full services, including engineering, geotechnical, pullout testing, field, and layout design services to address the actual site conditions of a project site. FLEXRACK by Qcells has completed over 5 GW of solar racking installations in over 40 U.S. states, 9 Canadian provinces and across the globe. Summary This position is responsible for the day-to-day administration, maintenance, support, and operation of FlexRack's IT infrastructure, systems, and end-user technology environment. The System Administrator serves as the primary technical resource for network administration, server administration, Microsoft 365 administration, cybersecurity, end-user support, onboarding/offboarding activities, and operational IT support across FlexRack locations. This role works closely with the Sr. IT Manager to maintain reliable and secure technology operations while supporting business continuity and organizational growth. This role is responsible for the tactical execution of IT operations while strategic planning, enterprise applications, vendor management, and ERP ownership remain with IT leadership. This position reports to the Sr.IT Manager, or another management personnel that the President of the Company may designate. Working hours are Monday through Friday, from 8:00am to 5:00pm or 9:00am to 6:00pm local time. Overtime and weekend working hours may be required as needed. This position is expected to travel up to 20%. Essential Job Function & Responsibilities Hardware Responsibilities End User Hardware Support Deploy, configure, and support desktop computers, laptops, docking stations, monitors, printers, scanners, mobile devices, and related peripherals. Diagnose and resolve hardware issues for end users. Coordinate hardware repairs, warranty claims, replacements, and vendor service requests. Maintain hardware inventories and asset tracking records. Prepare and deploy equipment for new employees and office relocations. Conference Room & Office Technology Support conference room technology, meeting room equipment, displays, cameras, audio equipment, and collaboration tools. Troubleshoot meeting-related technology issues. Coordinate technology setups for meetings, presentations, and training events. Onboarding & Offboarding Support Prepare and deploy workstations and equipment for new employees. Configure company-approved software and business applications. Recover and inventory equipment from departing employees. Assist with workspace technology setup and user orientation. Software Responsibilities End User Technical Support Provide Tier 1 and Tier 2 support for Microsoft Windows, Microsoft 365 applications, Teams, Outlook, SharePoint, and approved business applications. Troubleshoot software installation, configuration, printing, connectivity, and application-related issues. Escalate infrastructure, networking, security, and server-related issues appropriately. Microsoft 365 User Administration Create, modify, and disable user accounts as directed. Manage user permissions, distribution lists, security groups, and licensing assignments. Assist users with Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, OneDrive, and SharePoint functionality. Application Support Support approved business applications and user access requests. Assist with software deployments, upgrades, testing, and user training. Document recurring issues, solutions, procedures, and user support materials. Service Management Track, prioritize, and resolve user support requests. Maintain support documentation and knowledge base articles. Identify recurring issues and recommend process improvements. Coordinate with vendors, software providers, and corporate IT teams when necessary. Preferred Bachelor’s degree in Information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related discipline. Certifications CompTIA A+ CompTIA Network+ Microsoft 365 Fundamentals (MS-900) Technical Knowledge & Tools Hardware Desktop and laptop deployment Printer support Peripheral support Mobile device support Conference room technology Asset management Software Windows 10/11 Microsoft 365 Outlook Teams OneDrive SharePoint Basic Active Directory account administration Basic Entra ID account administration Software installation and configuration ERP systems Support Operations Ticketing systems User onboarding/offboarding Documentation User training and walkthroughs Relevant Experience Required 1-3 years of IT support, desktop support, service desk, or technical support experience. Preferred Manufacturing environment experience. Experience supporting multiple locations. Experience supporting Microsoft 365 environments. The CSSP provides continuous monitoring, threat detection, incident response, and vulnerability management across a complex, multi-tenant enterprise environment. Extensive experience developing and executing migration strategies for services, applications, or data moving from on-premises environments to hybrid or multi-cloud architectures. Strong knowledge and operational experience with Federal cybersecurity requirements and frameworks, including NIST, FISMA, and FedRAMP. Deep understanding of cybersecurity architecture, technical platforms, threat management, security controls, and industry best practices. Experience identifying security-relevant data and technologies across on-premises and cloud environments and developing technical solutions for evolving mission requirements. Experience evaluating vendors, designing technical solutions, and selecting cybersecurity technologies for enterprise implementation. Broad technical knowledge across enterprise IT, systems engineering, cybersecurity engineering, IT lifecycle methodologies, modernization, and transformation. Demonstrated ability to influence stakeholders and gain support for new technologies, concepts, practices, and approaches. Experience leading technical transformation and improving enterprise cybersecurity services and capabilities. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills with the ability to engage technical teams, Government stakeholders, and senior leadership. review_candidates.title: Lead Systems Engineer - GM Defense
review_candidates.description: Job Description The Role GM Defense delivers integrated vehicles, power and propulsion, and autonomy and connectivity solutions for global defense, security, and government customers. By leveraging GM’s advanced commercial vehicle platforms, engineering expertise, and large-scale manufacturing, GM Defense rapidly adapts proven technologies into military-grade, mission-ready solutions that help customers improve mobility, readiness, and sustainment while managing cost and complexity. System engineering is a multidisciplinary organization chartered with pulling together the highly complex and interconnected system that is the modern-day vehicle and related products. It transcends the physical nature of any specific design, cutting across traditional engineering disciplines to enable customer-focused execution of vehicle-level features. The Lead System Engineer is a people leader and technical expert role responsible for leading Systems Engineers in the definition and roll-down of system requirements, alignment of subsystem interfaces, and execution of verification planning to ensure the total product meets mission and program objectives. In this role, the Lead System Engineer provides system-level technical leadership across the product, integrating engineering inputs into a cohesive requirements-driven solution while ensuring safety, performance, timing, cost, and manufacturability targets are supported. Requirements and engineering inputs for this role may come directly from the customer as well as indirectly through the GMD business development team. AI-enabled tools are expected to be used in the development, refinement, and management of requirements, and the role is responsible for building team capability through required AI training and adoption of effective engineering practices. What You’ll Do Lead a team of Systems Engineers in development, decomposition, and roll-down of system requirements across the product Ensure subsystem requirements, interfaces, and verification plans are aligned to overall mission and program objectives Drive system-level integration across engineering disciplines to deliver a cohesive and executable product definition Lead cross-functional collaboration to ensure requirements support safety, performance, cost, timing, manufacturability, and validation objectives Oversee interface definition, requirements traceability, and verification planning across systems and subsystems Create System DFMEA and ensure system failure modes are understood, documented, and addressed through the design process Participate in Fault Tree Analysis and support development of the technical understanding needed to identify risk drivers and mitigation paths Collaborate on the V&V plan across mechanical, electrical, and controls domains to ensure the system is validated against requirements and intended performance Lead the integration and issue resolution of the system through the full development cycle Work with subsystem and component teams to optimize system design and improve total system performance Set availability targets, allocate them to subsystems and components, determine feature sensitivity to variation and failure modes, and define mitigation plans to improve performance to target Stay abreast of new technology, new processes, and new methods used to predict and improve availability Apply AI-enabled tools to improve the quality, speed, consistency, and traceability of requirements development Ensure the team receives required AI training and adopts AI tools and methods effectively within the systems engineering process Identify technical and integration risks early and lead resolution of cross-system issues that could impact program execution Support development of a scalable system architecture and requirements framework that can be successfully executed through development and launch Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications) BSE, BS in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent experience 10+ years professional experience in systems engineering, requirements development, product integration, or equivalent technical roles 5+ years of systems engineering experience within the defense industry, supporting the development, integration, and verification of complex defense systems Demonstrates effective interpersonal and communication skills to collaborate successfully with cross-functional teams, customers, and business development partners Strong understanding of engineering theory and principles of operation of mechanical, electrical, controls, and integrated vehicle systems Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams in requirements development, interface alignment, integration, and technical issue resolution Demonstrated ability to develop and execute System DFMEA, participate in Fault Tree Analysis, and collaborate on verification and validation planning Strong analytical ability to translate customer and product objectives into executable system requirements, availability targets, and mitigation plans Demonstrated technical and professional skills in systems engineering, including requirements management, traceability, risk identification, and cross-functional decision-making Ability to apply AI-enabled tools and methods to improve requirements quality, speed, consistency, and traceability while building team capability through effective adoption practices Candidate must be a U.S. Person (U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, asylee or refugee). Note: program participants are required to purchase/lease a qualifying GM vehicle every four years unless one of a limited number of exceptions applies. #GMD GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. The selected candidate will be required to travel <25% for this role. This job is not eligible for relocation benefits. Any relocation costs would be the responsibility of the selected candidate. review_candidates.title: Service Repair Engineer
review_candidates.description: Who We Are VITRONIC Machine Vision is the world's leading innovation driver for industrial image processing. VITRONIC develops specialized products and software for image-based quality inspection, identification, and process optimization. VITRONIC's forward-looking solutions help shape a safe and sustainable world. The limits of what is feasible are constantly being questioned to achieve the highest quality and productivity for companies in automotive, healthcare, transportation, automation, and logistics. Collaboration with our customers allow them to fully exploit technological capabilities and process efficiencies. Joint success forms the basis of long-term relationships with companies like BMW, Daimler, DHL, UPS, Toll Collect, Fresenius, and Sanofi, as well as public sector clients. Since its foundation in 1984, VITRONIC has consistently grown, with operations on five continents, over 80 countries, and approximately 1,300 employees. VITRONIC systems are developed and produced at the company headquarters in Wiesbaden, Germany. VITRONIC North America is headquartered in Louisville, KY. Position Overview VITRONIC Machine Vision is searching for a Service Repair Engineer. This technical engineer is responsible for maintenance, repair, diagnostics, and field reliability of automated traffic enforcement systems. This role supports the operational readiness and ongoing performance of roadside enforcement equipment, including speed and red-light camera systems, sensors, illumination units, routers, power components, housings, mounting structures, cabling, and related field infrastructure. The Service Repair Engineer will report to the Service Manager. Responsibilities Performs diagnostics, maintenance, repair, and service checks for installed enforcement systems. Troubleshoots cameras, sensors, flashes, routers, cabling, power, housings, mounting, and environmental conditions. Supports image quality and system performance investigations from a field perspective. Performs or supports alignment, calibration, inspection, component replacement, and repair activities. Documents service work, findings, parts used, risks, and required follow-up actions. Identifies recurring field issues and escalates them for problem management or engineering review. Supports preventive maintenance schedules, service manuals, troubleshooting procedures, and field checklists. Maintains service records, audit trails, calibration documentation, and repair history. Works with the Network Engineer when field issues may be caused by connectivity, configuration, signal quality, endpoint reachability, or secure access paths. Works with Technical Quality & Performance Managers when field trends, quality issues, recurring failures, or service performance concerns require investigation. Works with Implementation/Rollout Engineers during handover from deployment into regular operations. Supports urgent service issues when uptime, evidence quality, or customer commitments are affected. Minimum Qualifications Technical degree, technical certification, or equivalent practical experience in electronics, electrical systems, field service, mechatronics, industrial systems, or related equipment. Experience in field service, maintenance, repair, diagnostics, or technical troubleshooting. Ability to troubleshoot physical equipment and isolate likely causes of failure. Basic understanding of networking, routers, cabling, power, remote access, and monitoring feedback. Ability to work from technical documentation, wiring diagrams, checklists, and service procedures. Strong documentation habits and clear communication. Ability to work in field conditions and travel to customer or roadside locations as needed. Understanding of safety protocols and fieldwork best practices. Preferred Qualifications Experience with traffic enforcement, ALPR/ANPR, camera systems, LiDAR, radar, flash systems, telecom, utilities, smart city infrastructure, or public safety systems. Experience with Linux basics, device logs, remote access tools, network testing, or monitoring systems. Experience working with municipal, government, law enforcement, or regulated service environments. Experience supporting equipment installed outdoors, roadside, or in other public infrastructure environments. Benefits Health, Dental, and Vision coverage - company pays 90% Retirement Plan - Simple IRA and Roth IRA with competitive options Short-Term Disability Paid Vacation and Sick Days With your explicit consent which you provided as part of the application process, we will retain candidate personal data solely for the business purpose for which it was collected. VITRONIC Machine Vision Inc. is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status.

review_candidates.description: Support the trading technology and infrastructure of a fast-growing quantitative trading firm focused on sports and prediction markets. Founded five years ago, the firm has built its own proprietary data, statistical models, and pricing systems to generate trading opportunities across global betting exchanges and newer prediction markets. As an early mover in this space, the business has established a strong edge and continues to grow as larger trading firms begin entering the market. This DevOps Engineer role sits within a small, high-impact team responsible for scaling and maintaining the firm’s trading infrastructure. You will work closely with traders, developers, and data teams to ensure systems are running reliably, troubleshoot issues, and build automation and internal tools that improve efficiency across the organization. The environment is primarily Linux-based, with a focus on on-prem infrastructure while expanding further into the cloud. The stack includes Terraform for infrastructure provisioning, Ansible for configuration management, Grafana for monitoring and alerting, and growing adoption of Kubernetes, along with CI/CD pipelines. Exposure to SQL is helpful. The role involves a mix of support, automation, and infrastructure buildout in a fast-paced environment. The team operates on a hybrid model with a strong presence in Chicago, and the working schedule typically follows a 4-on, 4-off rotation, which may include weekends or later hours depending on major sporting events. Compensation ranges from $150,000 to $175,000, plus performance bonus and benefits.
